# `Browser.ScreenOrientation`

[Back to stdlib index](../stdlib.md)

Ipe.Browser.ScreenOrientation — lock/unlock the screen orientation and read
the current orientation, over `Ipe.Ffi.Js` ports.

A first-party proof of the per-capability web mechanism spanning BOTH port
directions: an outbound `JsCmd` requests a lock, unlocks, or queries the
current orientation; an inbound `JsMsg` carries the reply. Both cross the same
seal codec and fail-closed port discipline as every other port; there is no
second transport.

Importing this reserved `Ipe.Browser.<Api>` module discloses
`js-port:screen-orientation` (import-derived, keyed on the canonical
`Ipe.Browser.ScreenOrientation` path prefix via
`WebCapability::for_browser_module`, alias-immune); only the top-level app's
`[capabilities] accepts` set can grant it.

The two layers:

  * `Ipe.Browser.ScreenOrientation.Internals` publishes the closed
    outbound/inbound ADTs.
  * this module is the high-level layer: `lock`, `unlock`, and `current` are
    one-shot `Task`-shaped operations. The inbound `case` is EXHAUSTIVE: an
    unavailability or denial becomes a typed `Err`, never a silently dropped
    frame.

## `OrientationType`

The screen orientation type, matching the W3C Screen Orientation API.

  * `PortraitPrimary` — primary portrait (phone held upright).
  * `PortraitSecondary` — secondary portrait (phone held upside-down).
  * `LandscapePrimary` — primary landscape (phone rotated 90° clockwise).
  * `LandscapeSecondary` — secondary landscape (phone rotated 90° counter-clockwise).

## `lock`

```ipe
lock : OrientationType -> Task Error ()
```

`lock orientation` — lock the screen to the given orientation type, as a
`Task Error ()`.

Uses the correlated port→Task bridge (`Js.request`). Resolves with `Ok ()`
when the lock is applied; resolves with a typed `Err` when the API is absent
or the request is denied (e.g. not in fullscreen on some platforms).

Importing this module discloses `js-port:screen-orientation`; the app must
grant it with `accepts = [ JsPort ScreenOrientation ]` under [capabilities]
in package.ipe.

## `unlock`

```ipe
unlock : Task Error ()
```

`unlock` — unlock the screen orientation, allowing the device to rotate
freely, as a `Task Error ()`.

Resolves with `Ok ()` when unlocked; a typed `Err` when the API is absent.

## `current`

```ipe
current : Task Error OrientationType
```

`current` — read the current screen orientation type as a `Task Error OrientationType`.

Resolves with the current orientation; a typed `Err` when the API is absent
or returns an unrecognised type string.
